newsitem.title: USA: CSCE raises margins on coffee futures May 16.
newsitem.headline: CSCE raises margins on coffee futures May 16.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said on Thursday it raised the margins on May 1997 and July 1997 coffee "C" contracts to $8,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, effective May 16.
The previous margin required for May 1997 was $7,000, including a $3,000 spot charge, while the margin on July had been set at $6,000, including a $2,000 spot charge.
The margins required on all other coffee contracts will also be increased, rising by $1,000 to $5,000, the exchange said in a statement.

In addition, straddle or arbitrage transactions require a minimum of $1,500 for customers who are CSCE members or members of the trade. However, the $3,000 spot charge for May 1997 and July 1997 are applicable to all straddle and arbitrage transactions involving these months, the excahnge said.
For customers who are not exchange members or members of the trade, margins will be 140 percent above trade rates, the CSCE said.
